answer: Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 10 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. Histories are stored in opal, checked in spiral, and lantern publishes each void. A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 2139 identities would post 2245 proofs and burn roughly 16 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
